title: Planetarium view hotkeys swallow typing in the search field - object search by name is unusable from the keyboard
what_happened: With the planetarium plan panel open and the caret blinking in the 'Search objects, names...' field, typing 'Vega' deterministically leaves 'Va' in the field: the 'e' toggled the ecliptic layer on and the 'g' toggled the equatorial grid on instead of entering text. Typing the full lowercase alphabet 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' left only 'abd' in the field - c/e/f/g/h/m/n/r are all bound to view actions (constellation lines, ecliptic, FOV overlay, grid, reset view, minimap, now) and after 'h' (reset view) the field lost focus entirely so i..z were dropped too. Reproduced at 30ms, 250ms, 400ms and 2000ms inter-key delays: it is a shortcut conflict, not a dropped-keystroke race.
expected: A focused text field must consume ordinary character keys. Planetarium single-letter hotkeys should be suppressed whenever the primary focus is a text input (Flutter: check FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.context?.widget is EditableText, or move the shortcuts into a Shortcuts/Actions scope that a TextField's own shortcut scope shadows).
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > click the sidebar toggle (top right) > click the 'Search objects, names...' field > type Vega. Field shows 'Va'; the ecliptic line and the RA/Dec grid have both switched on behind the panel.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-11.png (grid + ecliptic appeared while typing 'Vega'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-18.png ('Va' after 400ms/char), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-19.png ('Va' after 2000ms/char), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-20.png ('abd' after typing the whole alphabet). Handler: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/planetarium_screen/actions.dart:507-624

title: At a 1-degree imaging FOV the sky renders essentially empty - measured 1 star in 0.6 sq deg at astronomical dark
what_happened: Zoomed to the minimum FOV (1.0 deg short axis), time set to tonight's astro dark via the TONIGHT button, view at the zenith (RA 17h44m, Dec +40, in Hercules): an 800x400 px patch of sky - 0.59 sq deg - contained ONE barely-visible dot (2 local maxima above grey level 40, zero above 60, on a background of 12). Star counts measured in the same pixel window while zooming out at the same sky centre: FOV 1.0 -> 1 star, 2.0 -> 6, 4.1 -> 33, 8.1 -> 74, 16.4 -> 328. Sky area scales as FOV^2, so surface density is flat at 1.7-3.5 stars/sq deg at every zoom - i.e. the depth never increases as you zoom in, and 2.9 stars/sq deg is exactly the whole bundled HYG catalog (119,600 stars over 41,253 sq deg), which is complete only to about mag 9.
expected: An imaging-scale field is the whole point of a planetarium inside an astrophotography app - it is what you check framing and guide stars against. At 1 deg it should show tens of stars. The bundled catalog is the binding constraint, not the FOV-adaptive magnitude ramp, which the code intends to add up to +7 mag by 1 deg.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > wheel-zoom to FOV 1.0 deg > press TONIGHT in the time bar > look at the sky.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/fov1-night2.png (the empty 800x400 field), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/fovzoom-2.png .. fovzoom-16.png (counts above). Bundled catalog: apps/desktop/.../assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1/tiles = 3,458,592 bytes over 768 tiles, ~28.7 bytes/star -> ~119,600 stars = full HYG.

title: Object info popup keeps the old object's name and coordinates but recomputes Alt/Az for the NEW selection - it said Deneb was 'Below Horizon' while Deneb was 11.5 deg up
what_happened: Clicked the star Deneb on the chart; the popup opened correctly (Deneb / HIP102098 / mag 1.3 / Star (A2Ia) / RA 20h 41m 25.9s / Dec +45d 16' 49" / Current Position 12.2 deg, Az 320.1 deg, badge 'Daylight'). Without closing it, I selected M57 from the search results. The view recentred on M57 (Center RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33d 01') and the selection ring moved, but the popup stayed open still headed 'Deneb' with Deneb's identifier, magnitude, spectral type and RA/Dec - while its 'Current Position' block changed to '-10.3 deg, Az 331.2 deg' with a red 'Below Horizon' badge. Independent computation for that instant (2026-08-02 14:51:01 UTC, 40N 105W): Deneb is at alt +11.46 deg, az 320.93 deg; M57 is at alt -10.33 deg, az 331.20 deg. The popup is therefore showing M57's horizon position under Deneb's name, to the 0.1 deg. It is not a one-frame race: 74 seconds later it still read Deneb / -10.4 deg / Az 331.4 deg, which again tracks M57 (-10.4 / 331.4) and not Deneb (+11.4 / 321.0). The popup also carries a 'Slew' button, so the object the user is reading about and the object the app considers selected are not the same thing at the moment they press it.
expected: The popup must either follow the new selection wholesale or close. Half-following - identity and catalogue coordinates from object A, live altitude/azimuth and the 'Below Horizon' warning from object B - is the worst of the three, because the visible result is a true-looking sentence about the wrong star.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium. Click a bright star (Deneb) to open its info popup. Leave it open. In the right panel's Search tab type '6720' and click the M57 result. The popup still says Deneb but its Current Position row now reports M57's altitude and azimuth and flags 'Below Horizon'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-26.png (popup for Deneb: Alt 12.2, Az 320.1, 'Daylight'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-33.png (after selecting M57: view centred at RA 18h53m35s Dec +33 01', popup still headed Deneb, Alt -10.3 Az 331.2 'Below Horizon'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-34.png (74 s later: Deneb, -10.4, Az 331.4, still 'Below Horizon'). Computed truth at 14:51:01 UTC from 40N/105W: Deneb +11.46/320.93, M57 -10.33/331.20.

title: Mouse-wheel zoom discards ~99% of scroll events - 172 notches move the FOV from 60 to 29 degrees
what_happened: Each wheel notch is supposed to zoom 1.15-1.2x. Measured live: 5 notches spaced 2.0s apart took FOV 28.9 -> 14.4 deg (exactly 1.15^5, correct). 12 notches spaced 0.3s took 60.0 -> 41.7 deg (the effect of ~2.6 notches). 120 notches spaced 0.05s took 34.7 -> 28.9 deg (the effect of ~1.3 notches out of 120). Spinning the wheel at any natural speed therefore barely zooms; it took 172 notches over two minutes to get from the default 60 deg to 28.9 deg, and there is no other zoom control on the desktop layout (no +/- buttons, no FOV field, and the '=' / '-' hotkeys are dead - see the focus finding).
expected: Successive wheel events must compound onto the pending zoom target, not restart the animation from the current (barely-moved) FOV. A user should reach an imaging FOV in a few flicks of the wheel.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > point at the sky > spin the wheel up 20 notches quickly, watch 'FOV (short axis)' in the bottom bar.

Source: _animateZoom sets _startFOV = current provider FOV and calls _zoomController.forward(from:0) on every event - packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/widgets/interactive_sky_view.dart:475-485,660-668

title: Alt/az readouts ignore precession - stated positions are up to 1.4 degrees off
what_happened: Clicking Capella at 18:38:16Z from 40N/105W/1650m the popup reported Alt 56.5, Az 295.7. Computing alt/az from the same J2000 RA/Dec with no precession gives 56.462/295.700 - an exact match; precessing to the equinox of date gives 56.804/295.681. Pollux at 18:39:17Z: app 76.0/214.0; J2000-direct 75.964/214.167; precessed 76.080/212.716 (1.45 deg of azimuth). So the horizontal transform uses J2000 coordinates unrotated, with no nutation, aberration or refraction either.
expected: Apply precession (and ideally refraction) before the horizontal transform. 26 years from J2000 is already ~22 arcmin of position, and the azimuth error near the zenith reaches 1.4 deg, which is enough to mis-call a meridian-flip or an obstruction check.
repro: Set the site to 40N 105W, open the planetarium at a known UTC, click Capella and Pollux, read 'Current Position'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-22.png (Capella: HYG118360, RA 5h16m40.7s Dec +45 59' 52", Alt 56.5 Az 295.7), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-24.png (Pollux: HIP37826, RA 7h45m17.7s Dec +28 1' 33", Alt 76.0 Az 214.0).

title: Moon is always drawn full and always labelled 'MOON 100%' - percent is fed into a 0-1 fraction and clamped
what_happened: On 2026-08-02 14:26:36 UTC from 40N/105W the planetarium drew the Moon as a solid, fully-lit white disc with the label 'MOON 100%'. The true illuminated fraction at that instant is 84.6% (independent Meeus computation, elongation 133.7 deg), and the app's own Dashboard Moon card says 'Waning Gibbous 84% illuminated' while Plan Tonight's target card says 'Moon is 79% illuminated'. Three surfaces, three different numbers, and the planetarium's is the one that is impossible. Root cause is a unit mismatch: AstronomyCalculations.moonIllumination() returns a PERCENT (0-100) and its doc comment says so, but SkyRenderer._drawMoon documents its third tuple element as 'illuminated fraction (0 = new, 1 = full)' and does rawIllumination.clamp(0.0, 1.0). Any real phase above 1% therefore clamps to exactly 1.0, so both the terminator geometry and the label are pinned at full moon for 29 of every 29.5 days. Only within a few hours of new moon does the value fall below 1 and render anything else - and then it renders a 1%-lit crescent as if it were 100%-scaled.
expected: The label should read the real illuminated percentage (84% here) and the disc should be drawn with the corresponding terminator, matching the Dashboard's Moon card.
repro: Settings > Location > lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium. The Moon glyph is near the default 0h/0deg view. Read its label; then compare with Dashboard > Moon card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-10.png (full white disc, label 'MOON 100%'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-02.png (Dashboard: 'Waning Gibbous 84% illuminated'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-07.png (Plan Tonight: 'Moon is 79% illuminated'). Source: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:761-785 returns 0-100; packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/rendering/sky_renderer/solar_system_and_markers.dart:481-486 clamps to 0..1 and :571 does (illumination * 100).round().

title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the night after tomorrow - every time is ~8 minutes wrong
what_happened: On 2026-08-02 at 40N/105W the Tonight sidebar listed IC311 with transit 09:24 and NGC6685 with transit 00:48. Selecting each object shows its coordinates in the bottom bar: IC311 = RA 3h16m46s Dec +40d00', NGC6685 = RA 18h39m58s Dec +39d58'. The true meridian crossings for those coordinates at lon -105 are 09:32 / 00:57 tonight (2026-08-02) and 09:28 / 00:53 the next night. The app's numbers match neither - they match 2026-08-04 (09:24 / 00:49), i.e. two sidereal days of drift. Root cause: bestTargetsProvider passes imagingTime = twilight.astronomicalDusk as the 'date', and at this site astronomical dusk falls at 00:00-00:02 LOCAL, so its calendar day is already tomorrow; calculateObjectVisibility then builds its search window as DateTime(date.year, date.month, date.day, 12) + 24h, i.e. noon TOMORROW to noon the day after. Whether the list slips a day therefore depends on whether dusk lands before or after local midnight, which flips with longitude-within-timezone, DST and season - so the same code is right in winter and a day out in summer. The app also contradicts itself on the same screen: with NGC6685 selected, the sidebar's Info tab reports 'Transit 00:52' for the very object whose Best-Targets card two tabs away says 00:48.
expected: The visibility window for 'tonight' should start at the local noon preceding the dusk being planned for (or simply take a night-start date, not a dusk timestamp). Transit for IC311 tonight is 09:32, not 09:24.
repro: Settings > Location > lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium > open the right sidebar > Tonight tab > scroll to 'Best Targets Tonight'. Note the transit time of a row, then click the row and read 'Center RA/Dec' in the bottom bar; compute the meridian crossing for that RA at that longitude.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-14.png (IC311 90 deg 09:24, NGC5311 19:58, NGC5313 19:59, IC4155 19:13, NGC6685 00:48), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-15.png (IC311 selected: Center RA 3h16m46s, Center Dec +40 00'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-16.png (NGC6685 selected: Center RA 18h39m58s, Center Dec +39 58'). Source: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/mosaic_targets.dart:145-159 and astronomy_calculations.dart:1024-1025. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-17.png (Info tab for NGC6685: Transit 00:52) against rp2-14.png (Best Targets card for NGC6685: 00:48).

title: The Alt/Az view toggle throws away where you were looking and jumps the chart to the zenith
what_happened: With the chart centred on M57 at a 2.0 deg imaging FOV (Center RA 18h53m35s, Center Dec +33d 01'), clicking the command bar's second icon - tooltip 'Alt/Az view - tap for Equatorial' - immediately recentred the chart on RA 4h42m52s / Dec +39d 59'. At the LST shown in the status bar (04:43) that is exactly the zenith: hour angle 0, declination equal to the site latitude of 40 deg. The framing on M57 was gone, at 2 deg FOV, with no undo. Clicking the toggle back to Equatorial restored RA 18h53m35s / +33d 01', and toggling to Alt/Az a second time again landed on the zenith (RA 4h43m52s / +39d 59' at LST 04:44), so it is deterministic, not a transient.
expected: Changing the coordinate frame is a change of grid, not a change of target. The same patch of sky should stay under the cursor, just with the horizon-aligned grid and the up-vector rotated - that is what Stellarium and SkySafari do. If the app genuinely cannot express the current centre in the alt/az frame (e.g. the target is below the horizon) it should say so rather than silently slewing the view.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > centre on any object and zoom to a narrow FOV > click the second command bar icon ('Alt/Az view'). Read Center RA / Center Dec in the bottom bar and compare with the LST in the status bar and the site latitude.

title: The app states three different, all-wrong depths for the bundled star catalog: 'mag <= 15.0', '~mag 11.5' and 'below mag 11.5 unavailable'
what_happened: Reached from the planetarium's Layers panel > Deep stars > Install, the Catalog Settings sheet describes the installed HYG Star Database as '119.6k objects, 32.4 MB, Version 4.2, Package Complete, Depth mag <= 15.0'. Two cards further down, the Deep-Star Tier card says the same bundled catalog's floor is '~mag 11.5'. The Layers panel itself says 'stars below mag 11.5 are unavailable'. All three are wrong in the same direction: 119,600 stars spread over 41,253 square degrees is 2.9 stars per square degree, and that is exactly the density I measured on screen (about 25 stars in a 3.8 x 2.0 deg field at FOV 2.0). A catalog complete to mag 15 would contain tens of millions of stars; HYG (Hipparcos + Yale BSC + Gliese) is complete to roughly magnitude 9. 'Package: Complete' next to 'Depth: mag <= 15.0' tells the user the empty field they are looking at is the real sky.
expected: State the completeness limit, not the faintest entry: about mag 9 for HYG. And make the three surfaces agree.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > command bar Layers icon > 'Deep stars (Tycho-2 / Gaia tier)' > Install > read the HYG card, then scroll to the Deep-Star Tier card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-51.png (HYG card: Objects 119.6k, Package Complete, Depth mag <= 15.0), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-56.png (Deep-Star Tier card: 'below the bundled HYG floor (~mag 11.5)'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-43.png (Layers panel: 'No tileset installed - stars below mag 11.5 are unavailable'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-37.png (the measured field at FOV 2.0).

title: 'Install' on the deep-star tier leads to a form asking the user to build and self-host a tileset - no tileset exists to install
what_happened: The Layers panel row 'Deep stars (Tycho-2 / Gaia tier)' carries a button labelled 'Install'. Pressing it opens Catalog Settings; scrolling to the matching card reveals 'Deep-Star Tier (Tycho-2 / Gaia)' with an empty 'Tileset base URL' text field, a Download button, and the line 'No official tileset is published yet - point this at a tileset you host yourself (see tools/catalog_prep in the Skotiq repository).' So the button named Install cannot install anything: the user is expected to clone the repo, run a catalog-preparation tool, and stand up a web server. Meanwhile the same row is what the app blames for the empty sky at imaging FOVs.
expected: Either publish and host the tileset (the DSS survey layer already proves the app can fetch remote sky data), or stop calling the button 'Install' - label it 'Configure source...' and say up front that no public tileset exists. As shipped this is the single biggest gap between what the planetarium claims and what it can draw.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > Layers > Install (on the Deep stars row) > scroll Catalog Settings to 'Deep-Star Tier (Tycho-2 / Gaia)'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-43.png (the Install button), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-56.png (the card it leads to, with the empty Tileset base URL field and the 'No official tileset is published yet' note).

title: Planets are computed for the equinox of date but stars and DSOs are drawn at J2000 - the two are mixed on one chart, so planets sit ~22 arcmin off the star background
what_happened: Clicking Jupiter on the chart at 2026-08-02 15:12 UTC from 40N/105W gave RA 8h 39m 30.9s, Dec +18d 53' 53", Alt 38.1, Az 96.9. An independent Keplerian ephemeris puts Jupiter at J2000 RA 8h37m58.3s / +18d59'31"; precessing that to the equinox of date gives 8h39m29.5s / +18d53'50", which matches the app to 1.4 s of RA and 3 arcsec of declination, and its alt/az (38.11 / 96.94) matches the app's to 0.01 deg - whereas the J2000 position gives 38.46 / 97.12, which does not. So the planet path precesses. The star path does not: the app reports Deneb as 20h 41m 25.9s / +45d 16' 49", which is its J2000 position to the tenth of a second, and its Alt/Az reproduces from those unprecessed coordinates. Both sets of coordinates are then fed to the same projection, so every planet is drawn displaced from the true stellar background by the accumulated precession since J2000 - about 1m32s of RA and 5.7 arcmin of declination here, roughly 22 arcmin total, or two-thirds of a Moon diameter. The screenshot shows this in the worst possible place: Jupiter is drawn right next to M44, the Beehive, and the drawn Jupiter-M44 separation is wrong by that amount.
expected: One reference frame for everything on the chart. Either precess the catalog to the epoch of observation before projecting (correct, and it also fixes the alt/az error already filed), or express the planetary ephemeris in J2000. Mixing them is worse than either.
repro: Settings > Location 40N 105W > Plan Tonight > Planetarium > press the home/reset icon so the zenith is centred > click Jupiter and read its Coordinates, then click a bright star and read its Coordinates. The planet is equinox-of-date, the star is J2000.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-66.png (Jupiter: RA 8h 39m 30.9s, Dec +18 53' 53", Alt 38.1, Az 96.9, drawn beside 'M44 - Beehive'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-26.png (Deneb: RA 20h 41m 25.9s, Dec +45 16' 49" = J2000 exactly). Computation: J2000 Jupiter 8h37m58.3s/+18d59'31"; precessed 8h39m29.5s/+18d53'50"; alt/az from precessed 38.11/96.94 vs from J2000 38.46/97.12.

title: Planets are typed as 'Star' in the object popup and written to the observation log that way, and the popup shows the internal id 'PLANET_Jupiter'
what_happened: Clicking Jupiter opens a popup headed 'Jupiter' with an identifier chip reading 'PLANET_Jupiter', 'mag -1.8' and a 'Type' field that says 'Star'. Logging an observation from that popup persists the same mistake: the row written to observation_logs is (object_name 'Jupiter', object_type 'star', catalog_id 'PLANET_Jupiter', ra 8.65857 h, dec 18.898, altitude 38.68, azimuth 97.48, rating 3, seeing good, transparency good, latitude 40, longitude -105). So the app's permanent observing record classifies a planet as a star, and the user-visible catalogue identifier is an internal enum token rather than a designation anyone would recognise.
expected: Type should read 'Planet' and the chip should show something meaningful (or nothing) rather than the internal key. object_type in observation_logs should be 'planet' so the log can later be filtered or exported (an observing log is data the user keeps for years).
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > press home to centre the zenith > click Jupiter. Read the Type row and the chip. Then Log Observation > Log Observation, and read the observation_logs table.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-67.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-69.png (popup: 'Jupiter', chip 'PLANET_Jupiter', 'Type: Star'). DB after saving: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-planetarium/data/skotiq.db 'select * from observation_logs' -> 1|1785683758|Jupiter|star|PLANET_Jupiter|8.65857259173372|18.8980441804957|38.6778254522709|97.4768462200507||3||good|good||40.0|-105.0

title: Your Sky says '1 region imaged' for a region that has zero frames, zero tiles and zero seconds of integration
what_happened: On a fresh profile with no captures at all, I used Your Sky > Name a region > Custom RA/Dec (RA 283.4, Dec 33.03, radius 0.5, name 'Ring Region'). The Regions header immediately read '1 region imaged'. Directly above it the Atlas coverage strip correctly reads 0s Integration / 0 Tiles / 0 Frames, and the region card itself reads '0s' and '0 tiles'. Naming a patch of sky is not imaging it, and the screen's own numbers say so.
expected: '1 region' (or '1 region, none imaged yet'). The count should say what it counts; 'imaged' is a claim about captured data that the same screen contradicts twice.
repro: Plan Tonight > Discover > Your Sky > Name a region > Custom RA/Dec > RA 283.4, Dec 33.03, name anything > Create region. Read the Regions header against the Atlas coverage tiles.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-77.png ('Atlas coverage 0s / 0 / 0' above 'Regions - 1 region imaged' above a card reading 'Ring Region  18h 54m . +33 02'  0s  0 tiles').

title: 'Name a region' keeps showing the validation error 'Pick a target first.' after you switch to the Custom RA/Dec mode that has no target to pick
what_happened: In Your Sky > Name a region the 'From a target' mode says 'No targets in your library yet - switch to Custom to enter a sky position by hand', yet Create region is enabled; pressing it produces the red error 'Pick a target first.'. Switching to the Custom RA/Dec mode as instructed leaves that error on screen, and it stays there while you fill in RA 283.4, Dec 33.03 and a name - i.e. the dialog is telling the user to do something the current mode does not offer, right up to the moment the region is created successfully.
expected: Clear the validation message when the mode changes or any field is edited, and disable Create region while the form cannot be submitted (rather than enabling it and explaining afterwards).
repro: Plan Tonight > Discover > Your Sky > Name a region > Create region (error appears) > switch to 'Custom RA/Dec' > fill RA/Dec/name. The error is still displayed.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-74.png (error in 'From a target' mode), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-75.png (still shown after switching to Custom RA/Dec), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-76.png (still shown with RA 283.4, Dec 33.03 and 'Ring Region' filled in).
